reasoning: Both outputs clear all four expectations and both ship harnesses that actually run — this was decided on verified claim integrity and on how much of the user's real problem each deliverable covers. I executed both. A's transcripts reproduce exactly (make red is deterministic; diagnose.py prints 506/506/497 with LOSS at enrich at 1.78%; drop_forensics separates DETERMINISTIC from STOCHASTIC on the shipped 14-night fixtures, including the honest self-flagged caveat that a 6.9x lift on 9 droppers is noise). But two of A's explicit claims about its own primary deliverables are false. A says 'ledger.py is delivered and has no dependency on my stand-in' and tells the user to 'Port this into your pipeline' — ledger.py has `import pipeline` at module scope, so copying it into a foreign directory raises ModuleNotFoundError on import (verified in /tmp). A also asserts a mutation check: 'deleting the lock ... each produces at least one failing test'; across 13 runs, deleting the lock leaves the suite at exactly the baseline 5 failed / 7 passed and test_ledger_accounts_correctly_under_the_concurrent_stage never goes red. In a document whose whole argument is 'do not report a proxy as the thing itself', asserting an unrun mutation result and a portability property that the file contradicts is the costliest possible error. B's numbers, by contrast, all held: GREEN/RED exits 0/1, MANGLED correctly identifying BRK.B and BF.B as renamed-and-deduplicated rather than dropped, backfill returning RUN-DEPENDENT on nights I generated myself, J=1.0 on both dropna and tail_batch, and tail_batch producing 54 drops (10.76%) exactly as the H4 rate-plausibility argument claims. Both of B's keep-forever modules (ticker_audit.py, stage_census.py) import and run standalone from an unrelated directory, which is what 'port this' has to mean. On substance B also covers more of the failure space: it is the only output that distinguishes a mangled symbol from a dropped one and that tracks `gained`/`dupes` so a stage resurrecting a stale row cannot hide a real loss behind a correct-looking total; it ships a working `replay` subcommand that turns a 1-in-50 nightly bug into 30/30 reds in one sitting rather than leaving replay as advice; and its question #3 (if the universe is regenerated nightly, 'the pipeline dropped it' and 'the universe builder never asked for it' look identical and have disjoint fixes) is the sharpest single insight in either document. B also carries the work through to a worked fix and a regression test at an explicitly argued seam, where A stops at diagnosis by design. A's compensating strength is real and I weighed it: it is the stricter of the two on expectation 1 — it refuses to rank causes at all, gating a signature-to-meaning table behind the instrument, where B does rank H1 as 'most likely'. But B builds and executes its loop to 30/30 reproduction in Phase 1 before any hypothesis appears in Phase 3, and re-ranks the whole list by what the measurement prints, so it satisfies the intent of that expectation rather than merely its letter. A spends noticeably more of its length on what it is refusing to do (the Iron Law block, the gate, the §7 refusal table) than B spends on the same discipline, and that budget came out of deliverable coverage.

Section 1 is the best single argument in either document for why 'no pattern' is a measurement gap: the 140-drop-events arithmetic, and the proxy trap that absence-at-the-end collapses five different bugs into one symptom

Section 2 ('Define red before building anything') is the cleaner articulation of the target: five non-negotiable properties stated before a line is written
Section 7's refusal table names real anti-patterns (retry the fetch, backfill from last night, alert on a threshold) and says why each destroys evidence
Repo greps for locating stage seams are practical and well chosen

strengths: Opens on the measurement, not on causes: 'You do not have a hypothesis problem. You have a measurement problem, and the measurement you need is already sitting on disk', followed by one command and 'Everything after this point is conditioned on what that prints'

Quantifies exactly how the eyeball misleads: in its own stochastic fixture 22% of drop events landed on a repeat offender by birthday-paradox coincidence, so the null baseline is what stops you inventing a pattern. This is the sharpest available answer to 'no pattern I can see'

Ships three loops at increasing cost, all executed and all verified by me: audit (51ms, exit 0/1, checked against an explicit red-capability checklist), backfill (per-night series plus verdict, reads step-vs-ramp for free), replay (30/30 red, --env sweeps for one-variable-at-a-time probes)
replay is the only real answer to 'a 2% bug is not debuggable one night at a time' — it converts one nightly sample into 30 in a sitting, which is what makes bisecting possible

Question #3 — if the universe is regenerated nightly rather than pinned, 'the pipeline dropped it' and 'the universe builder never asked for it' are indistinguishable in the output and have disjoint fixes — is the single most valuable observation in either document, and is correctly flagged as the assumption most worth resolving first

Hypotheses are gated on measurement, not asserted: the re-ranking table maps each backfill verdict to a new order and to hypotheses killed outright, and H4 is demoted on a quantitative rate argument (54 drops = 10.8% from the modulus, far off the observed 2%) that I reproduced
